verdict: Broadcom's revenue grew 29% to a record $19.3B as AI chip sales doubled to $8.4B, and 38 cents of every revenue dollar survived as net profit.

segments.name: Semiconductor solutions
segments.note: Chips — above all custom AI accelerators and networking gear for data centers. AI semiconductor revenue alone was $8.4B, up 106% YoY and above Broadcom's own forecast.

segments.name: Infrastructure software
segments.note: VMware and other enterprise software — the steady, subscription side of the company; growth was nearly flat here as the AI chips took the spotlight.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next chips and software — a smaller share of each revenue dollar than most chip rivals spend.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling the products and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization & restructuring
opex.note: Writing down the value of brands and technology bought in acquisitions (VMware above all) — a bookkeeping charge, not cash — plus restructuring costs.

takeaways.title: AI chips doubled
takeaways.text: AI semiconductor revenue hit $8.4B — more than double a year ago and above Broadcom's own forecast — on demand for custom AI accelerators and AI networking. Broadcom guided to $10.7B of AI chip revenue for the next quarter.

takeaways.title: Software barely grew
takeaways.text: Infrastructure software (mostly VMware) grew just 1% to $6.8B. Right now, essentially all of Broadcom's momentum is in silicon, not software.

takeaways.title: A cash machine
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $8.0B — 41% of revenue — because capital spending was only $250M. Few companies this size convert revenue into cash this efficiently.

oneTimers: GAAP profit carries $1,969M of amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets ($1,462M inside cost of revenue and $507M inside operating expenses) — mostly bookkeeping from the VMware deal, not cash. On Broadcom's non-GAAP view, net income was $10,185M instead of $7,349M.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $801M on Broadcom's debt, partly offset by $433M of other income — a net −$368M below operating profit.
